chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the people who drown in a ship or are crushed by a collapsing house, so they die, and it is not known who died before his companion. He said: 'They inherit from each other; such is how it is in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him).'
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdul Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj,
similar to it, except that he said: 'Such is how we found it in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him).'
ai.seo_question: How is inheritance distributed when multiple people die simultaneously and the order of death is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of mutual inheritance among a group who die simultaneously in a single event, such as drowning or being crushed, when the order of death is unknown. It explicitly links this legal ruling to the 'Book of Imam Ali (peace be upon him),' highlighting the continuity of jurisprudential authority from the Prophet's household. This ruling ensures that the estate is distributed fairly among the deceased's heirs rather than remaining in limbo, reflecting the practical application of Shia inheritance law.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the people who are drowning in the ship, or the house collapses upon them, so they are dying. So it is not know who has died before his companions’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They would inherit from each other, such is how it is in the Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup>’.
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj,
- similar to it, except that he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Such is how we<sup>asws</sup> have found it to be in the Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from ibn Mahbub from ‘ Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has narrated the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a people who drown with a ship or a house falls on them and they die; and it is not known who has died first. He (the Imam) said, ‘They inherit each other and that is how it is in the book of Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam.”’
Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al- Hajjaj
a similar Hadith except that he has said, ‘This is how we found in the book of Ali, Alayhi al- Salam.’
